bug.title: The dollar-neutral book's returns are never charged for turnover, so the uniform per-symbol fee cancels and every IR is gross
bug.symptoms: A signal with turnover 0.9 per rebalance and one with 0.1 get the same ir_standalone when their gross books match. Changing the fee rate changes nothing in the node metrics.
bug.reproduction_steps: Call compute_node_metrics on a priced panel where apply_costs charged 10 bps uniformly. Use two score paths with identical gross books: one constant ranks, one alternating ranks. ir_standalone and the book returns are identical.
bug.expected: - compute_node_metrics gains a keyword-only argument, cost_per_unit_traded: float = 0.0, a fraction of traded notional (0.001 is 10 bps). A negative or non-finite value raises EvaluatorMetricsError. - Each date's book return is the gross book return minus cost_per_unit_traded × traded_d. traded_d is Σ|w_d − w_prev|, where w_prev is the previous date's weights (absent symbols are 0). On the first book date, traded_d is Σ|w_d|. - book_returns, ir_standalone and everything derived from them are net. turnover keeps its definition (0.5·Σ|Δw|). - The default 0.0 reproduces today's figures exactly, so existing evaluator tests pass unchanged. - The module docstring states the formula and this spec's evidence: the uniform charge cancels in a centered book. - test_metrics_turnover_cost.py covers: - the reproduction above: with a cost, the high-turnover path's IR is lower by the expected amount - a hand-computed three-date example, including the entry charge - cost 0 equals the old figures - negative and NaN costs are refused It passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: the cost is charged per symbol, but in a dollar-neutral book it cancels. The traded-notional charge belongs where the weights exist, and that is in compute_node_metrics.
bug.constraints: Only the two listed files change NodeMetrics' fields and their validation are unchanged Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: evaluate_node and evaluate_on_dates never pass the venue fee to the book, so ir_tstat, cost_adjusted_ir and the close-out oos_ir are gross
bug.symptoms: A campaign's post-cost selection and close-out oos_ir are blind to turnover. The four M2 pivots' "post-cost" verdicts were gross.
bug.reproduction_steps: Evaluate one node twice over the same context, once with the fee schedule as configured and once with taker 0 bps. ir_tstat and cost_adjusted_ir are identical.
bug.expected: - Both compute_node_metrics call sites in _evaluate.py (evaluate_node ~:1397 and evaluate_on_dates ~:1644) pass cost_per_unit_traded = context.cost_schedule.fee_fraction(TAKER), the same rate _cost_schedule_from_context quotes. - ir_tstat, cost_adjusted_ir, the ScoreRecord and the node row are therefore net of turnover. Close-out oos_ir, which goes through evaluate_on_dates, is net as well. - Diagnostics: the node_evaluated event's score and the evaluate_on_dates result also carry ir_tstat_gross, computed with cost_per_unit_traded=0.0 over the same inputs. - The per-symbol apply_costs charge is unchanged. A comment at the schedule says it cancels in a centered book and that the turnover charge is the binding cost. - test_evaluate_turnover_cost.py covers: - the reproduction: with 10 bps, ir_tstat is below ir_tstat_gross for a turnover-bearing signal - a 0 bps schedule gives equal figures - evaluate_on_dates' result is net and carries the gross figure It passes under pytest-xdist. - Existing orchestrator tests are updated only where they pin a figure the charge changes; each keeps its intent. The orchestrator member suite (run at -n 2) and root tests/ pass.
bug.actual: Root cause: the evaluation pipeline hands compute_node_metrics no cost. The fee is applied only as a uniform per-symbol charge, and that cancels.
bug.constraints: closeout.py, _financial_eval.py and _process_pool.py are not edited; they reach the fix through evaluate_on_dates and evaluate_node No migration; stored rows are not rewritten Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
